import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import io

# Data provided as a string
data = """brand,model_year,megapixels,max_iso,weight_grams,price_usd,sensor_type,has_video_4k,lens_mount,body_type
Leica,2005,13.5,25600,324,811.8,Micro 4/3,1,E,Compact
Fuji,2019,46.4,51200,1151,3596.41,APS-C,0,EF,Mirrorless
Pentax,2012,38.7,12800,598,3357.2,Full Frame,0,MFT,Mirrorless
Olympus,2015,22.5,6400,1095,1555.7,APS-C,0,Z,Mirrorless
Leica,2016,12.2,25600,290,3899.09,Medium Format,0,MFT,DSLR
"""

# Read the data into a pandas DataFrame
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(data))

# Set a professional seaborn style
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="viridis")

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))

# Create a scatter plot to visualize relationships between key camera specs
# - X-axis: Megapixels (resolution)
# - Y-axis: Price (USD)
# - Hue: Brand (to distinguish manufacturers)
# - Size: Weight in grams (indicating portability/build)
# - Style: Sensor Type (fundamental camera characteristic)
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='brand',
    size='weight_grams',
    sizes=(100, 800),  # Adjust size range for better visual differentiation of weight
    style='sensor_type',
    palette='viridis',
    legend='full'
)

# Add annotations for each point to display the model year, providing more context
for i, row in df.iterrows():
    plt.text(
        row['megapixels'] + 0.5,  # Offset x-coordinate slightly for readability
        row['price_usd'] + 50,    # Offset y-coordinate slightly for readability
        f"{row['model_year']}",
        horizontalalignment='left',
        size='small',
        color='black',
        weight='semibold'
    )

# Add title and labels for clarity
plt.title('Camera Price vs. Megapixels by Brand, Weight, and Sensor Type (with Model Year)', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=12)

# Improve legend placement to avoid overlapping with data points
plt.legend(title='Camera Attributes', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels/legends from being cut off
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the plot to output.png
plt.savefig('output.png')
